metadata.hardware_requirements: The training process, presented in Figure 8, can be finished in less than 24 hours on a computing server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores).

nodes_source.source_quote: The data used to support the results of this study are available from the corresponding author upon request.
nodes_source.description: This refers to the experimental data used in the study, which includes traffic video data or derived simulation inputs based on real-world traffic.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: explicitly states 'available from the corresponding author upon request'

nodes_process.node_name: Extract Vehicle Locations and Form Position Matrix
nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices.
nodes_process.description: Raw traffic video frames are processed to extract vehicle (x,y) locations. These locations are then used to create a position matrix (mt) representing the traffic state at a given time step within a defined control area. Signal states are also encoded within this position matrix.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, no parameters for actual extraction specified, no tools stated for extraction

nodes_process.source_quote: Since one matrix is insufficient to describe vehicle dynamics, we stack the matrices of consecutive N time steps to represent the state s_t: S_t = {m_(t-(N-1)), ..., m_t}.
nodes_process.description: To capture vehicle dynamics effectively, position matrices from N consecutive time steps are stacked together to form the complete traffic state representation (St). Before stacking, down-sampling is applied to individual matrices to reduce input dimensions and maintain relevant information about vehicle positions, enhancing computational efficiency.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 2/2 params stated (deduced from text and table), no tools stated

nodes_process.source_quote: The ramp meter takes two possible actions at fixed decision time step L to determine whether the phase in the next time step is green (G) or red (R), namely, action set A = {G, R}.
nodes_process.description: This step defines the discrete action space for the ramp metering agent. The agent can choose one of two possible actions at each fixed decision time step L: set the traffic signal phase to green (G) or red (R) for the subsequent time step.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 1/1 param stated, action space clearly defined

nodes_process.node_name: Define Reward Function for DRL Agent
nodes_process.source_quote:
The reward r_t after action a_t is defined by the following: r_t = 
	v_t + 
	q_t, 
 > 0, 
 < 0,
nodes_process.description: The reward function for the DRL agent is designed to balance improving vehicle mobility on the mainline with reducing vehicle delays at the on-ramp. It is calculated as a linear combination of the average speed (vt) in the merging area and the average queue length (qt) at the on-ramp, using positive and negative weighting factors respectively.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all params stated, formula provided

nodes_process.source_quote: We adopt a deep neural network termed Q-network to approximate Q*(s, a). The neural network contains several convolutional layers and fully connected layers.
nodes_process.description: A deep neural network (Q-network) approximates the optimal action-value function Q*(s, a). This network, revised from Mnih et al. [30] to fit the specific input size (3x4x512 pixels), consists of three convolutional layers for feature extraction and two fully connected layers: one for Q-value estimation and another for predicting speed and queue length, supporting a multitask learning strategy. The network has about 2 million weights.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, most architecture parameters specified (Figure 7 and text)

nodes_process.node_name: Implement Multitask Learning and Loss Function
nodes_process.source_quote: A multitask learning strategy is implemented in the training process to improve learning efficiency. While training the ramp metering Q-network, the mean speed in the merging area and the queue length at the on-ramp are predicted simultaneously.
nodes_process.description: A multitask learning strategy is employed during training, where the Q-network simultaneously predicts the Q-value, mean speed in the merging area, and queue length at the on-ramp. The total loss function combines the primary Q-learning loss (L1) with a secondary loss (L2) that measures the prediction accuracy for speed and queue length, weighted by lambda.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all params stated, loss functions fully defined

nodes_process.source_quote: The algorithm for training the ramp metering policy is presented in Algorithm 1. The ramp meter takes new action with the e-greedy strategy...
nodes_process.description: The Deep Q-learning algorithm is trained to derive the optimal ramp metering policy. This process includes storing data in an experience replay buffer to decorrelate samples, using a target network for stable Q-value estimation, and employing an epsilon-greedy strategy for action selection to balance exploration and exploitation. The Adam optimizer updates network weights based on the total loss function.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all params stated (derived from Table 1 and text), all tools named or referenced

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator [31].
nodes_process.description: A microscopic traffic simulation environment is set up using SUMO to evaluate the DRL method. The simulation models a freeway section connecting Qingdao and Huangdao, defining road network topology and traffic conditions. Driving behavior parameters are calibrated using empirical data, and speed limits are specified for mainline and on-ramp segments.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all params stated, tool named

nodes_process.source_quote: The PI-ALINEA method fixes the length of the green phase and determines the length of the red phase in the current signal cycle based on the length of the red phase in the previous cycle and the downstream occupancies in the previous and current cycles.
nodes_process.description: For comparative evaluation, the PI-ALINEA ramp metering method is implemented as a baseline. This method uses a control formula that adjusts the red phase duration in a signal cycle, depending on the previous red phase length and downstream mainline occupancies. The green phase length is fixed. The goal is to regulate traffic to a predefined desired mainline occupancy.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3 (how green phase is fixed could be more explicit), all parameters stated, tool named

nodes_process.source_quote: The Q-network is trained in 10^6 training frames, and each scenario is evaluated in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_process.description: The trained DRL Q-network and the PI-ALINEA baseline are evaluated against a no-control scenario. Training is performed for 10^6 frames, and each scenario undergoes 20 simulation experiments, with each simulation initialized with different random seeds. The computations are carried out on specified GPU and CPU hardware.
tools_mentioned: Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, key parameters stated, hardware mentioned

nodes_process.source_quote: The results demonstrate that, in comparison with a state-of-the-practice method, the proposed DRL method results in (1) lower travel times in the mainline, (2) shorter vehicle queues at the on-ramp, and (3) higher traffic flows downstream of the merging area.
nodes_process.description: This step involves analyzing and presenting the outcomes of the simulation experiments. Comparisons are drawn between the DRL method, PI-ALINEA, and a no-control scenario, focusing on key performance indicators such as mainline travel times, on-ramp queue lengths, traffic flows downstream of the merging area, and speed distributions. Results are visualized through various figures and tables.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, outputs are specific figures/tables, no explicit tools or params

nodes_process.node_name: Conduct Perturbation Analysis of Video Data
nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data.
nodes_process.description: To evaluate the DRL method's reliance on specific information from video data, a perturbation analysis is conducted. The control area is segmented into eight distinct subareas. For each subarea, its information is selectively removed from the original video data to generate perturbed inputs. Simulation experiments are then performed with these perturbed datasets, and travel times are analyzed.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, method fully described, key parameter stated
